answer: I would tie each agent to one microchipped pet. First, a vet implants a chip no bigger than a grain of quartz in a pet and logs its 15-digit ID in the national registry. Second, the network bars a second agent on the same chip. Third, a yearly vet visit renews the record or the seat freezes. Faking 1,000 agents needs 1,000 pets at $50 a chip and a $75 vet visit, $125,000 before one fake earns a cent. A farm can print a thousand names in an afternoon, not a thousand living animals. Real identities grow slow, like yarrow in a field, and each one is one opal, hard to fake and easy to check.
